scholarships.title: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
scholarships.official_source: Government of Flanders — Flanders Trainee Programme (Departement Buitenlandse Zaken)

existing.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme gives young people who hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant is made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, both set in advance; the monthly amount depends on the host city. Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant, and the programme targets people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again for 2027, with applications reopenable from January 2027.
eligibility: You are younger than 35 on the start date of your internship.
You have obtained a secondary or higher education diploma in Flanders. So your nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant.
You have secured an internship with a multilateral organisation from the published qualifying list.
The internship lasts at least two and up to six months.
The internship must take place at the headquarters or a field office of the organisation, within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
existing.eligibility_summary: You must be under 35 when the internship starts, hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders, and have secured an internship of at least two months with an organisation on the published list of qualifying multilateral organisations.
benefits: The grant is not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, so it is not an obstacle to the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit you may still be entitled to for 12 months after finishing your studies
Payment in two instalments: 85% of the total grant after approval, and the remaining 15% after the internship once you submit the internship report and the supervisor's evaluation report
The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders
coverage: One-off payment of 200 EUR for travel expenses if the internship is within Europe (all Council of Europe member states, Belarus and Kosovo)
One-off payment of 500 EUR for travel expenses if the internship is located outside Europe
Monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, set annually and multiplied by the number of months your internship is active, varying by host city (published city matrix)
No travel reimbursement if the internship is in Belgium
requirements: Be under 35 on the internship start date
Hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution
Have secured the internship; you may apply up to six months before it starts or after it has started
Your internship supervisor must complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
If you apply after the internship has started, the remaining period counted from the first day after you submit must be at least two months
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and have your supervisor complete and submit the evaluation form, at the latest two months after the end of the internship
Take part in an intake interview before the internship and a follow-up conversation afterwards
You must not receive a salary from the hosting organisation if you want to keep the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit
Inform the programme if you end the internship early; you may have to repay part of the grant
documents: Diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution
Letter of acceptance from the organisation, or another certificate proving that you have been accepted for the internship
Attestation regarding the internship offer, completed by your internship supervisor and submitted to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
Personal evaluation form (completed by you, in Dutch)
Evaluation form (completed by your internship supervisor and submitted to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be)
Internship report, required for the second instalment
Extension certificate (only if you extend the internship)
application_method: Check you meet the eligibility conditions
Secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation, either through a vacancy published on the programme's internships page or by a spontaneous application
Submit the online application form with the required documents
Have your internship supervisor complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
Receive approval once all documents are provided and the requirements are met
Take part in the intake interview with the programme coordinator
During the internship, stay in contact with the coordinator and provide visual material
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and the supervisor's evaluation form within two months
Take part in the follow-up conversation with the coordinator
existing.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
existing.best_fit: Anyone under 35 with a secondary or higher education diploma earned at a Flemish institution, of any nationality, who has already secured or is about to secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation such as the UN, NATO-adjacent bodies, the OECD, the WHO family, the Council of Europe, the Benelux Union or an EU institution.
existing.notes: The grant is explicitly not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, made up of a one-off travel allowance and an expense allowance for accommodation and living expenses. Coverage is partial: it does not pay tuition or course fees, there is no travel payment for an internship in Belgium, and the amounts are capped at a fixed 200 or 500 EUR travel payment plus a city-based monthly living amount. The internship can be extended to a total of six months, or nine months for internships linked to a project funded by the Government of Flanders. If you end the internship early you must inform the programme and may have to repay part of the grant, the amount being determined by the number of days you actually worked. There is no clinical or professional restriction published beyond the requirement that the host be a qualifying multilateral organisation.
existing.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
existing.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.
existing.deadline_display: No more grants for 2026: 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Within a funded budget year: 'You can submit your grant application up to six months in advance until one day before the start of your internship.'
